audience_description: A SaaS founder, growth marketer, or product strategist in the B2B expense management or fintech space who wants to understand how Expensya pivoted from a global self-serve GTM to a regional sales-assisted model — to evaluate whether a similar geographic/GTM specialization strategy would work for their own product.
recommended_h1_format: How [Company] Shifted From Global Self-Serve to Regional Sales: A Homepage Teardown
secondary_keywords: B2B SaaS sales-assisted vs self-serve positioning
content_angle: Focus on the STRATEGIC DECISION BEHIND the pivot — why retreat from English/global/free-trial positioning to French/regional/demo-only. The searcher is not looking for a surface-level 'what changed' list; they want to understand the market signals, customer feedback, or unit economics that likely drove Expensya to double down on French-speaking finance teams and replace self-serve with sales assistance. Emphasize the trade-offs: broader TAM vs. higher-intent conversion, brand accessibility vs. regional compliance expertise.
what_the_searcher_wants: Validation or cautionary evidence for their own GTM narrowing decision. They want to know: Did Expensya's retreat from broad positioning actually work? What metrics or messaging cues suggest this was the right move? Would a similar play succeed in my own niche or geography?
what_to_avoid: Treating this as a generic 'homepage before/after' comparison. Do NOT just list the HTML changes or describe the visual design differences. Avoid shallow observations like 'they added more French text' without explaining WHY (compliance, regulatory pressure, market saturation in English-speaking segments). Do NOT ignore the GTM funnel change (free trial → demo request) — this is the core insight and should anchor the entire analysis.
